fields.title: Adopt from the beadwork review
fields.description: Follow-ups from inspecting jallum/beadwork (2026-10-07). Its storage and sync design (orphan branch, tree as state, intent replay) is not adopted; these product ideas are.

fields.title: bp prime / bp onboard: agent instructions emitted by the binary
fields.description: bw onboard prints a snippet for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; bw prime prints the workflow context an agent loads at session start. The instructions version with the binary. Ours: how to find work (ready), claim before starting, comment progress, close with a reason, sync before stopping, what provisional/unconfirmed mean. Biggest adoption lever: agents do not use what they do not know.

fields.title: bp recap: what happened since I last looked, across repos
fields.description: Cursor-driven, incremental activity view like bw recap, but with what our journals carry: machine, agent, thread, branch and commit per event. Cross-repo over every store under BP_HOME. The view the owner opens every morning on a multi-machine setup.

fields.title: bp ready <parent>: scope the frontier to a subtree
fields.description: bw ready <parent-id> returns only actionable descendants. Matches how agents work an epic.

fields.title: bp close --recursive: close a subtree leaf-up in one transaction
fields.description: Children before parents, already-closed ones skipped, one locked write. Owner-ended claims publish at once as today.

fields.title: Migration page: from br/bd to bp and back
fields.description: br export | bp import - ; bp export | br import. State that bp keeps Beads field names (owner, issue_type) where beadwork renames them, so round trips are lossless. Note comment ids from 2^47 and what br does with them.

fields.title: CI on the repository: check.sh as the workflow
fields.description: Run ./check.sh on push and PR (fast modules); --stress nightly or on demand. Reviewers then cite a commit and a green run instead of a SHA-256 of bp.

fields.title: Format upgrade path: FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED is only half a migration story
fields.description: bp refuses a newer manifest untouched (Q04). Before a format 2 ever exists we need the upgrade command (bw upgrade repo is the reference): who migrates, how older clients are told, and how a half-migrated remote is detected.

fields.title: Name the project and create its GitHub repository
fields.description: beads-poc is a working name. beadwork is taken by a direct neighbour (jallum/beadwork). Candidates checked free on crates.io, PyPI and both GitHub accounts: beadroll (preferred), claimjar, abaci. Decide the account too: bpcakes (next to another project) or a personal account. Then first commit, gh repo create, add origin, bp sync.

fields.description: Deferred until the project is open-sourced. For the four machines we have, bead is one Python>=3.10 file copied to ~/.local/bin (where br lives; on PATH everywhere except linux-2). Decided 2026-10-08: do the minimal pieces now (bead --version, install/deploy script); packaging (pyproject.toml, uv tool install from the git URL, pipx), a release process and versioned builds when the repository goes public.

data.reason: Closed with a policy rather than machinery: format 1 is frozen and changes are additive; an older bead sets aside events it cannot apply, reports them, carries them through sync untouched and applies them after an upgrade (FormatPolicy test). A breaking change, if ever needed, follows writers-lag-readers via the manifest. README 'Format and upgrades', REVIEWING section 2.

fields.description: Deferred with roll-ydfw. The adversarial review of the package proposal (2026-10-08) found 12 module-level cycles under a 17-module cut and 562 cross-module call sites; the agreed plan is: relocate the six misplaced helpers (stamp, b36, hung_up, the OVERVIEW/PRIME/ONBOARD texts, merged_into_default, forget_receipts/receipts), then split coarse: base (errors, text/JSON io, git runner, URLs), machine (store, workspace, identity), model (validation, journal, replay, graph, presentation), sync (writes, link, protocol: where every test patch target lives), commands, cli. Keep 'from .x import name'; patch at use sites. Split finer only where a module outgrows ~800 lines. Packaging itself is done (27d16d3).
fields.title: Coarse module split (4-6 modules along measured seams) at the open-source milestone

fields.description: Seen once in the six-machine 2400-operation stress model (step 2297, a sync on machine 1 failed with GIT_ERROR; the rerun of that sync succeeded, fsck clean, integrity 0). The preserved sync.git had 4 packs and 5 loose objects, so git's auto gc (gc.autoDetach) had repacked it in the background several times during the run; a mktree/hash-object/commit-tree racing the repack's deletion of loose objects is the probable cause (the same shape as the review's V8_PruneOnThePrivateSyncRepo, which saw 'git mktree: fatal: entry ... is unavailable'). Pre-dates the package split (no git behaviour changed). Proposed fix: bead owns sync.git, so set gc.auto=0 there and run the maintenance itself under the store lock (repack -d when loose objects pass a threshold), never detached; keep origin's receive-side gc as the remote's business. Needs a test that provokes the race.
fields.title: sync.git runs git's detached auto-gc; a concurrent bead command can hit a vanished loose object (transient GIT_ERROR)

data.reason: Done: beadroll/ with base, machine, model, queries, sync, commands, cli (9d52d31 + 2db2699); generated from the one file by name, function bodies unchanged, imports strictly downward; ./bead launcher re-exports the package for drivers; tests.support.patched for in-process tests. data.text: Correction: the close reason said drive 10/10; the summary was 9/10 with S2 FAIL. Reopened until S2 is understood.

fields.description: Found by the GitHub drive on linux-1 (2026-10-08): ~/.local/state/beads-poc-test/<ws>/sync.git holds 13 zero-length loose object files (mode 0444, written in two bursts at 18:16:42 and 18:16:49 +0200) and two tmp_pack_* leftovers; git fsck: 'object file ... is empty', 'missing object ... for refs/beads/remote'; every fetch fails with 'fatal: cannot read existing object info' / 'fetch-pack: invalid index-pack output', which bead reports as REMOTE_UNREACHABLE although the remote is fine. sync.git is a derived cache: journals live in events/, attempts in pending/, and the remote holds everything published, so bead can recover on its own: when fetch fails with a local object error, move sync.git aside (sync.git.damaged-<time_ns>), re-create it and fetch again, under the store lock; report what it did. Root cause of the empty objects still unknown (a SIGKILLed fetch leaves tmp files, not empty finals); check linux-1's git version and fsync settings.
fields.title: A damaged private sync.git (empty loose objects, leftover tmp packs) makes every sync fail as REMOTE_UNREACHABLE; bead should rebuild it

data.text: Probe on linux-1: git 2.43.0, no core.fsync*/gc.auto settings; the two tmp_pack_* files date from 18:59 (fetches aborting on the already-empty objects, not the original cause); the 13 empty objects (18:16:42 and 18:16:49) remain unexplained. Fix implemented: Link.fetch/git raise SYNC_REPO_DAMAGED on git's local read errors (never on relayed 'remote:' lines); synchronise and coordinated set sync.git aside as sync.git.damaged-<time> under the lock and retry once; sync reports sync_repo_rebuilt, info lists damaged_sync_repos. Tests: SyncRepoDamage (2).

data.reason: Fixed in 0a3df73: git's local read errors in sync.git are SYNC_REPO_DAMAGED; synchronise and coordinated set the repository aside as sync.git.damaged-<time> under the lock and retry once; sync reports sync_repo_rebuilt, info lists the copies. Verified on the real damaged store on linux-1 (13 empty objects): the next sync rebuilt it, pulled 2, pushed 1, integrity 0. Root cause of the empty objects not established (git 2.43.0, no fsync/gc settings).

Done: beadroll/ with base, machine, model, queries, sync, commands, cli (9d52d31 + 2db2699), generated from the one file by name, function bodies unchanged, imports strictly downward; ./bead launcher re-exports the package for drivers; tests.support.patched for in-process tests. Fast baseline 434 OK; stress model and sweep OK (one transient GIT_ERROR on the first stress run, the auto-gc race in roll-zc49); drive 10/10 on the installed builds of all four machines (after fixing S2's criterion, 6eb58c8, and the sync.git rebuild, 0a3df73).

data.text: Containment for the unexplained empty objects: bead never writes into objects/ itself; every loose object came from git (hash-object/mktree/commit-tree under the lock, or fetch's unpack-objects) or from git's detached gc. Now fetch.unpackLimit=1 keeps fetched objects in index-pack's verified packs, git's auto gc is off in sync.git, bead repacks under the lock, and pack-level read errors count as local damage (rebuild). If empty objects recur, the only remaining writer is bead's own hash-object/mktree/commit-tree under the lock.

data.reason: Fixed in a440bfb: git's automatic maintenance is off in sync.git (gc.auto=0, no detached gc, maintenance.auto=false; fetch.unpackLimit=1 keeps fetched objects packed), carried in the link's environment so every existing store gets it; bead repacks under the store lock once loose objects or packs pile up and prunes only unreachable loose objects older than an hour. Tests: SyncRepoMaintenance (2). Fast baseline 436 OK, stress model + sweep OK.

Done: .github/workflows/check.yml runs ./check.sh on every push and pull request (Ubuntu on Python 3.12/3.13/3.14, macOS on 3.14) and the stress models plus the protocol sweep nightly or on request. First fully green run: https://github.com/bpcakes/beadroll/actions/runs/37852426542. Three things the runners found and that were fixed on the way: check.sh now prints each failure's assertion line; the V7 oracle skips the upper-case-scheme shape on a git (2.43) that refuses it; the prune property accepts SYNC_REPO_DAMAGED as transient.

Done: MIGRATING.md, the procedure as run on a real tracker (227 issues): bead init --import publishes at once; check with info, a canonical export comparison and ready/blocked against br; the two non-obvious steps (imported in_progress issues have no owner; .beads/ and the br lines in AGENTS.md are history, bead onboard replaces them); nothing to do on the other machines but bead sync; several projects at once; and the way back through bead export. Linked from the README.

fields.description:
Found in the 2026-10-09 project health check on main e0041ec. tests/test_sweep.py:484-486 filters failures whose (op, fault, pair) belongs to G12_SCHEDULES even though G12 is marked fixed in docs/FINDINGS.md. The default ten-schedule SLICE contains none of the ten G12 schedules. Dedicated tests in G12_RetriedEndOfClaimIsPublished cover the basic bug, but full-sweep coverage still silently permits these failures.

Reproduction, without running the protocol: with scratch BEAD_HOME, import tests.test_sweep; set BEAD_SWEEP=full; mock schedules() to return [('close', 'crash-before-push', 'OR')]; mock run_schedule() to return {'ok': False, 'op': 'close', 'fault': 'crash-before-push', 'pair': 'OR', 'violations': ['simulated recurrence of fixed G12']}; run Sweep('test_sweep') using unittest.TestResult. Actual result: wasSuccessful() is True, with zero failures and zero errors. This demonstrates a test guard gap, not an observed production recurrence.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Remove the obsolete G12 failure exemption so every failing full-sweep schedule fails the test; update the stale comments/docstring; include representative G12 retry schedules in regular coverage; demonstrate that an injected failing G12 result makes the sweep fail and the real G12 regressions pass.

fields.description:
Found in the 2026-10-09 project health check on main e0041ec. check.sh:32 runs python3 infra/roundtrip.py | tail -1 || status=1 under /bin/sh. The pipeline status is tail's status, so a failed roundtrip.py is ignored when tail succeeds.

Reproduction: copy check.sh into a temporary directory and put a stub python3 first on PATH. For -m unittest invocations, have it print a successful summary and exit 0; for the roundtrip invocation, print simulated roundtrip failure to stderr and exit 17. Run the scratch check.sh --real with a scratch BEAD_HOME. Actual: stderr reports the simulated roundtrip failure but check.sh exits 0. No real exports or remotes are used by the reproduction.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Preserve and propagate the roundtrip process exit status independently of tail; keep the summary output; verify a simulated failing roundtrip causes a nonzero check.sh --real exit and a successful roundtrip still exits zero, using scratch data only.
fields.title: Propagate round-trip failures from check.sh --real

data.text:
Health check, 2026-10-09, main e0041ec: this issue's original one-file/Python 3.10 description is stale. The repository is now a seven-module stdlib-only package requiring Python >=3.11, with pyproject.toml, installation instructions, both licenses, and a release procedure. Built wheel and sdist from an archived HEAD in scratch space; both installed cleanly in isolated Python 3.13 environments and passed a two-machine create/claim/refused competing claim/comment/close/sync/export smoke check.

Release remains unpublished: repository visibility is PRIVATE; GitHub reports no tags or releases; PyPI's beadroll JSON endpoint returns 404. Rescope the remaining work to publication and versioned artifacts, and add a build/install smoke check to CI. Before making the existing repository public, review historical machine identifiers: commit 075e269 still has the four-entry HOSTS dictionary in infra/drive.py (including a concrete SSH target); the hygiene test scans current tracked files only. This is a disclosure choice for the maintainer, not evidence of a credential leak. The local checkout was not modified by the health check.

Project health check, 2026-10-09, main e0041ec: the working tree is clean and the installed bead package matches all nine checkout Python files. Fresh ./check.sh passed, 441 tests and no skips/failures:
  test_hygiene: 1 test, 0.057s
  test_replay: 60 tests, 57.106s
  test_storage: 9 tests, 16.278s
  test_compat: 4 tests, 58.591s (local real Beads compatibility exercised)
  test_commands: 106 tests, 295.053s
  test_protocol: 54 tests, 336.748s
  test_hardening: 207 tests, 751.907s
Current main CI is green on Linux Python 3.11-3.14 and macOS 3.14: https://github.com/bpcakes/beadroll/actions/runs/37908446972 . The most recent stress run passed on a985eb0: https://github.com/bpcakes/beadroll/actions/runs/37855144265 ; this ran the randomized models and default ten-schedule slice, not the full 660-schedule sweep. This check-in did not rerun the stress suite or the real multi-machine infrastructure drives.

Two verified P2 check/reporting gaps are filed with reproductions and acceptance criteria: roll-dih8.8 (obsolete G12 exemptions in the full sweep) and roll-dih8.9 (check.sh --real masks a failed roundtrip.py exit). No implementation files were changed. Package wheel and sdist build/install/two-machine smoke checks passed in scratch space; remaining release work is noted on roll-ydfw. Tracker sync is healthy: no pending ownership, waiting events, integrity errors or unpublished work.

Housekeeping before more feature work: roll-dih8.2/.3/.4 lack acceptance criteria; AGENTS.md:98 still points to the removed beadroll.py instead of beadroll/cli.py.

Removed the G12 failure exemption from the full sweep and added close-before-publish/retry/sync and delete-before-publish/other-actor/retry scenarios to the default slice (12 scenarios). Added fast guard regressions in tests/test_check.py: all ten formerly exempt injected failures fail the sweep in full and default modes, passing results still pass, and the default slice includes both interrupted owner transitions. The new tests failed before the fix and pass after it. Actual sweep and dedicated G12 recovery regressions are running; the full baseline will follow. The pre-change baseline was the 441-test green run at unchanged e0041ec from this same session.

The checker now captures the roundtrip process status before summarizing stdout and prints the full report on failure. Tracing the path also showed infra/roundtrip.py returned zero after failed import/export/ready commands or differing records; fixed its exit status too so the check is meaningful end to end. Synthetic subprocess and roundtrip-driver regressions reproduced those failures before editing and now pass. Updated README, reviewing instructions, changelog and findings ledger. data.text:
Audit of roll-dih8.3, 2026-10-09, main a455383050e40c75b202cd33141de6d0098461b1. Scope: inspect the feature and existing query behavior; no source edits or feature implementation.

Verdict: the P2 feature is justified and still unimplemented. The issue currently has only a one-sentence description and no acceptance criteria. The graph and existing readiness predicate already support an additive query implementation; no event-format, storage, sync or ownership-protocol change is needed.

Verified observations:
1. bead ready PARENT --json exits 2 with USAGE (unrecognized arguments). cli.py:256-258 has only --epic and the shared flags. cmd_ready at commands.py:563-571 aliases --epic to --parent, and select at :547-549 matches immediate parents only. With epic E -> nested epic N -> task T, global ready contains T but both ready --epic E and ready --parent E return []. The same omission affects ready descendants below closed or deferred intermediate parents. This is the feature gap already tracked here, not a new duplicate issue.
2. P2 validation defect: scope IDs are resolved inside the candidate loop after other filters. On an initialized empty tracker, ready --epic missing and ready --parent missing both succeed with []; on a populated tracker the former raises ISSUE_NOT_FOUND, but adding --label absent makes it succeed with [] again. A typo can therefore masquerade as an exhausted work queue. Resolve a supplied scope before filtering, even when there are no candidates. select is shared with list, so a fix there must preserve direct-parent membership.
3. API ambiguity: supplying --parent A --epic B silently ignores B (commands.py:566). In the fixture A had two ready children, only one shared with B; the command returned both. Define selector compatibility before adding a third spelling.

Proposed acceptance criteria (recommendations from this audit, not implemented):
- bead ready [PARENT] adds optional recursive scope. Without PARENT, output and behavior stay as they are. Accept any issue type as the root and the same full/prefix-omitted IDs that State.resolve accepts. A missing root always reports ISSUE_NOT_FOUND.
- Membership is the strict transitive closure of parent-child edges, excluding the root and deduplicating immutable issue UIDs. Use actual edges, not the display-key prefix (an imported ex-root.99 with no edge must stay out). Walk every parent link in multi-parent graphs and terminate on merged/imported cycles and deep chains.
- Traverse through intermediate issues regardless of status, ownership, type, label, or other output filters. In the 16-issue fixture, the recursive result should contain ex-leaf, ex-shared, ex-below-closed and ex-below-deferred. Their containing nodes need not themselves be ready.
- Readiness is the existing predicate evaluated against the full State: open, no confirmed claim, no status conflict, and no blockers. An ancestor or a second parent outside the selected subtree still contributes blockers. Do not redefine readiness as leaves only: a ready non-epic parent and its ready child can both appear. Preserve provisional-claim and disputed-status behavior.
- Apply existing user filters and deterministic ordering (priority, created_at, id), then the limit. Keep the ready JSON array/text output and read-only/no-network behavior. --limit 0 remains unlimited.
- Recommended compatibility choice: keep existing --parent and --epic as direct-child selectors; make the new positional form recursive. Explain the distinction in help/prime and README. Reject simultaneous scope selectors instead of silently discarding one. If --epic is to become recursive, that needs an explicit documented compatibility decision rather than an incidental change to select.

Implementation boundaries: add the positional parser argument in cli.py; put an iterative descendant query in queries.py using State.children (model.py:362-369); filter membership in cmd_ready while using the full state for readiness. Do not reuse reaches/waits_for: waits_for also follows blocking dependencies and would put out-of-scope prerequisites in the subtree. The descendant query may later serve roll-dih8.4, but this feature does not depend on recursive close. Record the final semantics in docs/REVIEWING.md section 2 and README; add behavioral regressions and a FINDINGS row for the validation defect when fixed.

Regression coverage to add during implementation: nested epics and non-epic parents; full and prefix-omitted root IDs; valid leaf root; absent root with empty/filtered-out candidates; multiple parents and diamond deduplication; cycles including the root and a chain beyond the recursion limit; closed/deferred/claimed intermediates; external ancestor blockers; status conflicts and claims; filters/order/limit after scope; misleading dotted IDs; legacy selectors and conflicting selectors; JSON/text and unchanged exports.

Validation completed in this audit:
- 6 existing focused tests passed: BpTest.test_readiness_follows_the_rule_br_uses; ReplayAuditBugs.test_second_parent_blockers_hold_child; ReplayAuditProperties.test_tombstoned_blocker_unblocks_unless_status_disputed; ReplayReaudit.test_merged_parent_cycle_matches_br_readiness; Review5CLI.test_e11_parent_filter_matches_every_direct_parent; Review6.test_prime_matches_ready_and_help_outside_a_repository_is_silent.
- 12 synthetic CLI probes in a Sandbox with its own BEAD_HOME, repository and local bare remote reproduced the cases above. Imports were offline; exports before/after query probes were identical. An initial scratch assertion expected VALIDATION for the positional parser failure; the observed code was USAGE, the assertion was corrected, and the complete probe run passed.
- Full baseline/stress not rerun for this source-unchanged, scope-limited audit. The prior implementation/validation session is recorded on roll-dih8.8/.9. Working tree remains clean.

Minimal reproductions (run only in a scratch repository with a scratch BEAD_HOME): init --prefix ex --offline; create E -t epic --offline; create N -t epic --parent E_ID --offline; create T --parent N_ID --offline. Then compare ready --json (contains T) with ready --epic E_ID --json ([]), and ready E_ID --json (USAGE). On that populated tracker compare ready --epic missing --json (ISSUE_NOT_FOUND) with ready --epic missing --label absent --json ([]).

Audit complete. The implementation remains open; release the audit claim so the work can be picked up with these findings. P2 priority remains appropriate.

Decision, 2026-10-09, from the maintainer (asked in this session, with br 0.5.7's behaviour as evidence): bead ready --epic ID becomes recursive like br's (br documents --epic as 'sugar for --parent <id> --recursive, depth-unbounded and cycle-safe' and refuses --epic with --parent). The new positional bead ready ID means the same: ready issues anywhere beneath ID. --parent ID stays direct children only, as in br's ready --parent and bead's list --parent. No -r/--recursive flag. This overrides the audit's recommendation to keep --epic direct-only. Probed in a scratch repo: br ready --epic E excludes the root (also when the root sits in a parent cycle), walks through closed and deferred intermediates and every parent link, keeps second-parent blockers from outside the subtree, accepts a prefix-omitted root, returns [] for a leaf root, and reports ISSUE_NOT_FOUND for a missing one; bead's global ready matched br's on the same fixture.

data.reason: Done in e9ec582 on main (committed locally, not yet pushed). bead ready ID and bead ready --epic ID (as in br) are ID's subtree: every issue beneath it through parent-child edges, at any depth and through every parent link, whatever lies in between; the root is excluded; parent loops and a 1,100-level chain terminate. Readiness is judged on the whole tracker. --parent stays direct children, in ready and list. Audit defects fixed: a scope is resolved before filtering (ISSUE_NOT_FOUND, list --parent too), and ID/--epic/--parent are mutually exclusive, each given once (USAGE). Docs: README, REVIEWING.md section 2 (the --epic decision), FINDINGS J01-J03, CHANGELOG. Fast baseline green (455 tests); Codex review (gpt-6-astra, xhigh, read-only) of a455383..e9ec582 found no actionable defects.
